- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at +3–4 points above recent peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price has been trending upward for 5+ days, forecast tends to drop too soon; delay downward correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.67.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.67 to -0.33 in 3 days), model fails to adjust; apply smoothing filter to avoid abrupt direction changes.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day window (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.0 point bias upward for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
